q: Motion along a straight line is called _____ motion.
e: Motion along a straight line is called linear motion. Linear names motion along a straight line. Circular: a round path, which is not the uniform-medium light path.

q: In linear motion with constant velocity, the acceleration is _____.
e: In linear motion with constant velocity, the acceleration is zero. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: The equation of motion for a linear motion with constant velocity is $v =$ _____.
e: The equation of motion for a linear motion with constant velocity is $v =$ $\frac{s}{t}$. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: If the rate of change of velocity is constant, the acceleration is said to be _____.
e: If the rate of change of velocity is constant, the acceleration is said to be constant. Constant here means a quantity that does not change, not the agreed measuring unit. Variable: a quantity that can change, not the agreed measuring unit.

q: The first equation of motion for constant acceleration is $v =$ _____.
e: The first equation of motion for constant acceleration is $v =$ $v_0 + at$. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: The equation $v^2 = v_0^2 + 2as$ relates final velocity, initial velocity, acceleration, and _____.
e: The equation $v^2 = v_0^2 + 2as$ relates final velocity, initial velocity, acceleration, and displacement. Displacement here means the straight directed change from start point to end point. Time: the duration of an event, not the distance moved along a force.

q: The equation for displacement in constant acceleration motion is $s =$ _____.
e: The equation for displacement in constant acceleration motion is $s =$ $v_0 t + \frac{1}{2}at^2$. Displacement can be smaller than the path if the path bends.

q: The average velocity $\bar{v}$ in constant acceleration motion is given by $\bar{v} =$ _____.
e: The average velocity $\bar{v}$ in constant acceleration motion is given by $\bar{v} =$ $\frac{v_0 + v}{2}$. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: In the MKS/SI system, the unit of displacement is _____.
e: In the MKS/SI system, the unit of displacement is m. SI writes every quantity as a number times an agreed unit.

q: In the CGS system, the unit of velocity is _____.
e: In the CGS system, the unit of velocity is cm s$^{-1}$. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: In the FPS system, the unit of acceleration is _____.
e: In the FPS system, the unit of acceleration is ft s$^{-2}$. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: The unit m s$^{-1}$ is read as _____.
e: The unit m s$^{-1}$ is read as metre per second. The physics in this sentence is built around metre per second.

q: In a linear motion, the magnitude of the displacement is _____ to the distance moved.
e: In a linear motion, the magnitude of the displacement is equal to the distance moved. Displacement can be smaller than the path if the path bends.

q: As the body is moving with a non-varying velocity, the instantaneous velocity and average velocity are the _____.
e: As the body is moving with a non-varying velocity, the instantaneous velocity and average velocity are the same. Same here means lined up together, which is how a bar becomes magnetised.

q: In the equations of motion, we will use positive (+) and negative (-) signs to describe the two _____ directions along a straight line.
e: In the equations of motion, we will use positive (+) and negative (-) signs to describe the two opposite directions along a straight line. The physics in this sentence is built around opposite.

q: Except Eq. (2.7), the rest equations of motion can be expressed in _____ form.
e: Except Eq. (2.7), the rest equations of motion can be expressed in vector form. Vector here means a quantity that has both magnitude and direction. Scalar: a quantity that has magnitude only.
Eq. (2.7) and Eq. (2.8) are derived from Eqs. (2.6), (2.9) and (2.10).

q: The instantaneous acceleration $a$ is defined as $a = \lim_{\Delta t \to 0} \frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t} =$ _____.
e: The instantaneous acceleration $a$ is defined as $a = \lim_{\Delta t \to 0} \frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t} =$ $\frac{dv}{dt}$. Acceleration is not velocity. It is how velocity is changing.

q: A body moving with a constant acceleration of 5 m s$^{-2}$ changes its velocity by _____ in every second.
e: A body moving with a constant acceleration of 5 m s$^{-2}$ changes its velocity by 5 m s$^{-1}$ in every second. Velocity is directed. Speed is the size of that velocity.

q: The speedometer of a car indicates the _____ speed of the car.
e: The speedometer of a car indicates the instantaneous speed of the car. A speedometer reading is the speed at that instant, not the trip average.

q: When a body is moving along a straight line with a constant speed, the velocity of the body is also constant because its magnitude and direction remain _____.
e: When a body is moving along a straight line with a constant speed, the velocity of the body is also constant because its magnitude and direction remain constant. Constant here means a quantity that does not change, not the agreed measuring unit. Variable: a quantity that can change, not the agreed measuring unit.
